Subject: Re: Sizing question for dedicated inference

Hi Sergio — thanks for taking this on. Quick context on our expected usage so you can size the Dedicated pool: we expect to move our core assistant from the hosted pilot to a dedicated slab if the economics and latency hold up. Current projected signals (monthly) — these are conservative estimates from product: 500K inference calls / month; average input tokens ~85; average generation ~215 (so ~300 tokens / call). Daily profile is uneven: steady baseline ~1.8 calls/sec globally, but peak windows (US business hours) could run as high as 38 calls/sec sustained for 2–3 hours.

Key SLO: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for prompt+generation (we can tolerate slightly higher tail with a fallback to a cheaper model).

Other notes: we do a small amount of embeddings for search (not on this slab) and expect traffic to be fairly bursty around morning and after product releases. Procurement asked us to share a usage sheet — attached.

— Megan
Product Lead, Acuity Labs

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Acuity slab sizing — need a short capacity brief

Forwarding Acuity profile (see attachment). Megan’s ask is straightforward but we should be explicit in assumptions. Ask: can you produce a 1-page capacity brief + a conservative dedicated recommendation by Friday? Key constraints: p95 <= 350ms; peak sustained window ~38 rps for 2–3 hours; baseline 1.8 rps; average tokens per call ~300.

Notes for the model: Acuity prefers Redwood-rw-13B-q4 for parity with their dev tests, but they said they’re open to a smaller model for non-critical traffic. Give two scenarios: (A) parity model (rw-13B-q4) and (B) lower-cost quantized 7B variant with fallback. Include required GPUs, expected tokens/sec headroom, and an ops playbook for cold starts / cache warmup.

— Sergio

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acuity slab sizing — first-pass numbers

Team — first pass calculations below (simple, conservative math + safety factor). I used the hourly distribution and treated the 38 calls/sec as sustained peak for sizing headroom.

Assumptions: average tokens per request = 300. tokens/sec at peak = requests/sec * tokens_per_request. We model p95 SLO using in-cloud single-model latencies measured in our lab for rw-13B-q4: median token latency = 0.0009s/token, tail multiplier ~1.7x at p95 under load (this is service-level measurement, not end-to-end).

Scenario A — rw-13B-q4 (parity):
- Peak tokens/sec = 38 * 300 = 11,400 tps
- Measured throughput per H100-80GB worker (single-process, conservative): ~3,800 tps sustained at our p95 latency target
- Required workers (no safety): 11,400 / 3,800 = 3.0 -> round up to 4 workers to avoid CPU/GPU contention
- Add ops safety (spare capacity + warm-up): +1 worker -> recommended pool = 5 workers (H100-80GB).
- Expected p95 latency (modeled): ~320–340ms (fits SLO with narrow buffer).

Scenario B — rw-7B-q4 (cost-optimized fallback):
- Peak tokens/sec same = 11,400 tps
- Throughput per H100 worker (7B) = ~7,500 tps (7B is lighter)
- Required workers = 11,400 / 7,500 = 1.52 -> round up to 2 workers
- Recommend primary pool: 3 x H100 for 7B (primary) + 1 x H100 for rw-13B can be used as a canary/critical-path model if desired — but Ops risk is higher if you use 7B only.

Operational recommendation: start with Scenario A reserved slab of 5 H100-80GB workers for the first 60–90 days. Configure automated overflow to hosted rw-7B fallback during unpredicted surges (we estimate fallback cut-in at 85% utilization). Add a warm cache strategy to pre-warm KV caches before the morning peak (pre-roll ~20 minutes).

Risks & notes:
- The per-worker throughput numbers depend strongly on q4 kernel performance and sequence length distribution (we used 1k context upper-bound). If Acuity’s response sizes spike higher, throughput per worker will drop ~15–25% — call this out in the summary.
- If they require strict p99 bounds, we should add another spare worker (5 -> 6) or lower the primary model to 7B for non-critical routes.

I’ll assemble a 1-page brief and a slide with cost estimates (monthly committed vs. burst). Attaching a quick estimate PDF.

— Ben
